rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic إن and lām answer disbelievers who imagine that, had God wanted faith, He would have compelled them; they use this excuse for idolatry.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر ب { إن } ولام الابتداء يومىء إلى أن هذا كالجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: على with a noun and verbal meaning conveys obligation: God undertakes guidance by grace and wisdom, first creating moral discernment, then sending messengers to clarify, remind, and guide before reckoning.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( على ) إذا وقع بين اسم وما يدل على فعل يفيد معنى اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that both lives belong to God completes the reminder that guidance is a favor; all things in both realms are His, so people have no claim upon Him beyond what He grants.
rows.anchor: وعطف { وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى } على جملة : { إن علينا للهدى } تتميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recompense in the next life follows God's disclosed ordering; worldly causes and effects are also His arrangement, and whoever neglects its safeguards deserves the consequences.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة عظيمة إلى أن أمور الجزاء في الأخرى تجري على ما رتبه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā may simply continue the discourse if the earlier warning is literal past speech; it introduces a detailed warning branching from the preceding general warning.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الفاء لمجرد التفريع الذكري

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Exegetes agree the first referent is Abu Bakr, after he freed Bilal; idolaters slandered that he repaid a favor owed by Bilal, and the verse refutes them.
rows.anchor: اتفق أهل التأويل على أن أول مقصود بهذه الصلة أبو بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr is one instance within the general description of a giver seeking purification; mentioning this unusual case does not restrict the general wording.
rows.anchor: وهذا شبيه بذكر بعض أفراد العام وهو لا يخصص للعموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عنده is a locative metaphor for a favor firmly attached to its recipient, as though the favor were near him in place.
rows.anchor: و { عنده } ظرف مكان وهو مستعمل هنا مجازا في تمكن المعنى

rows.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
rows.claim: The cited line uses عنده for an established good held with someone, illustrating Ibn Ashur's locative-metaphor explanation.
rows.anchor: قال الحارث بن حلزة : من لنا عنده من الخير آيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min is an added particle after negation, intensifying the denial that anyone has a favor to repay.
rows.anchor: و { من نعمة } اسم { ما } النافية جر ب { من } الزائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected: the giver has no repayable favor, but seeks God's countenance; seeking is a more earnest form of request than baghy.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في { إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه } منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's face means His essence, so seeking His essence means seeking His approval.
rows.anchor: والوجه مستعمل مرادا به الذات كقوله تعالى : { ويبقى وجه ربك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of abundant reward completes the statement that the most God-fearing will be kept from Hell, adding the good things prepared for him.
rows.anchor: وعد بالثواب الجزيل الذي يرضى صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawfa secures the promise in the future, extending the recipient's contentment through future time; lām al-ibtidāʾ further emphasizes the report.
rows.anchor: وحرف ( سوف ) لتحقيق الوعد في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This compact expression encompasses everything people desire.
rows.anchor: وهذه من جوامع الكلم لأنها يندرج تحتها كل ما يرغب فيه الراغبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conflicting occasion reports suggest narrators lacked clarity; Ibn Ashur supposes the second revelation pause lasted about twelve days, to give the Prophet respite and build capacity for revelation.
rows.anchor: فالذي نظنه أن احتباس الوحي في هذه المرة كان لمدة نحو من اثني عشر يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reconciles reports by proposing a first pause of forty days, a second of roughly twelve, and the present surah as the third revelation, when practice of arduous work develops; this also reconciles reports about al-Muddaththir.
rows.anchor: فيكون نزول سورة الضحى هو النزول الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of qalaa is omitted because waddaka makes it clear, a verbal ellipsis also seen in the following verbs awa, hada, and aghna.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { قلى } لدلالة { ودعك } عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is an independent continuation of the opening oath clauses, not its answer: after denying abandonment, it reassures that the Prophet's ending will surpass his beginning in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: والجملة معطوفة على الجمل الابتدائية وليست معطوفة على جملة جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite forms al-ākhirah and al-ūlā generalize the statement into a concluding maxim that includes ongoing revelation and other forms of good.
rows.anchor: وما في تعريف ( الآخرة ) و { الأولى } من التعميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms may denote the afterlife and worldly life, promising eternal good, while also describing the Prophet's circumstances as progressing from one state to a better one.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون المراد هنا من كلا اللفظين كلا معنييه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes both lām particles as lām al-ibtidāʾ and supplies an omitted subject in the second clause: 'You will surely be given by your Lord.'
rows.anchor: جزم صاحب ( الكشاف ) بأنه لام الابتداء وقدر مبتدأ محذوفا

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib regards the lām in 'your Lord will give you' as the emphatic lām answering an oath; Ibn Hisham agrees, apparently because the future particle prevents nūn of emphasis.
rows.anchor: واختار ابن الحاجب أن اللام في { ولسوف يعطيك ربك } لام التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur questions the claim that the future particle itself forces the lām to be an oath-response lām.
rows.anchor: وأقول في كون وجود حرف التنفيس يوجب كون اللام لام جواب قسم محل نظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The childhood-care account proves the promise is certain: God's steady care from the Prophet's beginnings cannot be coincidence, and reassures believers while warning opponents that the promise will occur.
rows.anchor: استئناف مسوق مساق الدليل على تحقق الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question expects assent; wajada means encountered, takes one object, and yatiim, dallan, and aa'il are circumstantial states in an image of aid given to someone in distress.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري ، وفعل { يجدك } مضارع وجد بمعنى ألفى وصادف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan is a child whose father has died; the Prophet's father died before his birth or very early in infancy.
rows.anchor: واليتيم : الصبي الذي مات أبوه وقد كان أبو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poor person lacks wealth; God enriched the Prophet inwardly with a contented heart and materially by inspiring Khadija to enter a commercial partnership with him.
rows.anchor: والعائل : الذي لا مال له ، والفقر يسمى عيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of awa, hada, and aghna are omitted because the preceding second-person pronoun supplies them; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وحذفت مفاعيل { فآوى } ، { فهدى } ، { فأغنى } للعلم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first fā is explicative; amma implies 'whatever the case,' while an understood condition means that acknowledging God's favors entails gratitude, now detailed in three commands.
rows.anchor: الفاء الأولى فصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three gratitude practices may follow a matching, ordered weave: care for orphans answers being sheltered, especially on Sufyan ibn Uyayna's reading of the questioner as seeking religious guidance.
rows.anchor: وقد قوبلت النعم الثلاث المتفرع عليها هذا التفصيل بثلاثة أعمال تقابلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphan is the object of 'do not subdue' and is fronted for emphasis; the construction also separates amma from its fā-marked result, with fronting marking the focus of concern.
rows.anchor: واليتيم مفعول لفعل { فلا تقهر } . وقدم للاهتمام بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on mistreating an orphan echoes the caution not even to say 'ugh' to parents and to speak gently when unable to give.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { فلا تقل لهما أف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qahr means overpowering or humiliating, by conduct, speech, or even a scowling gesture; corrective discipline for a child's welfare remains a caregiver's right.
rows.anchor: والقهر : الغلبة والإذلال وهو المناسب هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioner corresponds to the Prophet once lost and seeking a way; because an inquirer may face a foolish rebuff, gratitude for guidance requires patience and generosity toward all seekers.
rows.anchor: لأن الضلال يستعدي السؤال عن الطريق

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b's verse illustrates a companion's evasive, discourteous answer to someone seeking help.
rows.anchor: كما قال كعب : وقال كل خليل كنت آمله

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna interprets the generic questioner as including those asking for religious guidance, not only material charity.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا التفسير عن سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs that people will follow the community and seekers will arrive from distant lands to learn religion, so they should be treated well; Abu Sa'id welcomed visitors as fulfilling this advice.
rows.anchor: روى الترمذي عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sa'il is a generic definite, covering anyone who asks the Prophet about what is appropriate to ask him.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { السائل } تعريف الجنس فيعم كل سائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the questioner instead means a known petitioner for charity, the command answers God's enrichment of the Prophet; this is a disordered weave, as al-Kashshaf reads it.
rows.anchor: فإن فسر { السائل } بسائل معروف كان مقابل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr is verbal rebuke, such as telling someone to go away; banning it also rules out harsher abuse, blows, theft, and leaving someone needy, but not correcting breaches of Islamic etiquette in asking.
rows.anchor: والنهر : الزجر بالقول مثل أن يقول : إليك عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking of God's favor answers material enrichment: reveal the blessing and acknowledge God's generosity; the generic wording extends gratitude to all favors.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث } مقابل قوله : { ووجدك عائلا فأغنى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative disordered weave, the questioner matches material enrichment and speaking of the blessing instead matches guidance to true religion.
rows.anchor: وكان المراد بنعمة ربه نعمة الهداية إلى الدين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahdith means informing others in acknowledgment of God's favor; bringing the prepositional phrase forward focuses attention, as in the two preceding commands.
rows.anchor: والتحديث : الإخبار ، أي أخبر بما أنعم الله عليك اعترافا بفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is directly commanded and the imperative originally entails obligation; the community shares the orphan and questioner prohibitions under the equality principle, supported by other evidence.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم فمقتضى الأمر في المواضع الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community's duty to publicize blessings needs balancing: some favors, such as prophethood and Qur'an, are unique to the Prophet, and publicizing others' blessings may invite ostentation or hurt the deprived.
rows.anchor: وأما مساواة الأمة له في الأمر بالتحدث بنعمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must announce his messengerhood as part of conveying the message, and should identify the obedience owed him; he can speak of blessings without fear of ostentation.
rows.anchor: وهو تبليغه الناس أنه رسول من الله وأن الله أوحى إليه وذلك داخل في تبليغ الرسالة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: When asked to describe himself after praising the Companions, Ali first cited the ban on self-praise, then invoked this verse: if asked he gives, otherwise he begins; he has abundant knowledge to share.
rows.anchor: وفي ( تفسير الفخر ) : سئل أمير المؤمنين علي رضي الله عنه عن الصحابة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid restricts 'your Lord's favor' to the blessings of Qur'an and prophethood.
rows.anchor: نعمة القرآن ونعمة النبوءة وقاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو نضرة
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Abu Nadra that speaking of God's blessings is obligatory.
rows.anchor: ومن العلماء من رأى وجوب التحدث بالنعمة . رواه الطبري عن أبي نضرة

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the address is to the Prophet while its ruling applies generally; Qadi Iyad characterizes it as specific to him yet general for his community.
rows.anchor: وقال القرطبي : الخطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم والحكم عام له ولغيره

rows.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
rows.claim: Amr ibn Maymun would tell a trusted brother how much prayer God enabled him to do the previous night.
rows.anchor: وعن عمرو بن ميمون : إذا لقي الرجل من إخوانه من يثق به

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن غالب
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Ghalib reported his worship each morning as a gift from God and defended this practice by the verse.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن غالب : أنه كان إذا أصبح يقول : لقد رزقني الله البارحة

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
rows.claim: Abu Raja al-Utaridi likewise told Ayyub about his night prayers and praise, which Ayyub bore from him.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن العربي عن أيوب قال : دخلت على أبي رجاء العطاردي

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi allows reports of worship to trusted friends when sincere, but warns that sharing deeds can become ostentation or invite suspicion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي : إن التحدث بالعمل يكون بإخلاص من النية عند أهل الثقة

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Ali recommends telling a trusted brother when one receives or does good; al-Fakhr says this is suitable only without ostentation and when it may inspire imitation.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفخر والقرطبي عن الحسن بن علي : إذا أصبت خيرا أوعملت خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden was removed in part by guidance to truth, which ended the Prophet's distress over his people, and by provision for a livelihood that could distract him from reflection on reform.
rows.anchor: وأما وضع الوزر عنه فحاصل بأمرين : بهدايته إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the Prophet's mention is a metaphor for causing people to remember him well by creating the means of his reputation; he was known for exceptional virtues and called al-Amin.
rows.anchor: ورفع الذكر مجاز في إلهام الناس لأن يذكروه بخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His name's pairing with God's name in the profession of faith is a supreme instance of raised mention; Qur'an 81:19–21 may also refer to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ومن عظيم رفع ذكره أن اسمه مقترن باسم الله تعالى في كلمة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri transmits a Prophetic interpretation of raised mention; al-Suyuti grades its Ibn Hibban and Abu Ya'la chain fair, while Qadi Iyad cites it without a chain.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا التفسير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث أبي سعيد الخدري عند ابن حبان وأبي يعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addition of لك with 'raised' parallels 'expanded for you'; عنك with 'removed your burden' also signals care while supplying the needed complement and a vague-then-specific effect.
rows.anchor: والقول في ذكر كلمة { لك } مع { ورفعنا } كالقول في ذكر نظيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā makes explicit an understood inference: since ease accompanies hardship, it cancels hardship's effect, alluding to God's past care and promising its continuation.
rows.anchor: الفاء فصيحة تفصح عن كلام مقدر يدل عليه الاستفهام التقريري هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faraghta implies that the person was occupied; leaving a task means completing it. The object is omitted because the context points to the Prophet's demanding mission.
rows.anchor: وفعل فرغ يفيد أن فاعله كان مملوءا بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing one major task, the Prophet should undertake another, filling his time with important work; fansab is the main command, while 'when free' prepares and sequences that work.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى إذا أتممت عملا من مهام الأعمال فأقبل على عمل آخر

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet, returning from an expedition, called the return a move from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند قفوله من إحدى غزواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early exegetes differ only by examples of what task is completed; omission gives the contextual category broad scope, including work prioritized as possible, as prayer alongside fighting shows.
rows.anchor: واختلفت أقوال المفسرين من السلف في تعيين المفروغ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule includes the Prophet's particular duties: night prayer, jihad when Muslims are strong, and managing communal affairs; fronting the time clause emphasizes sequential work.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحكم ينسحب على كل عمل ممكن من أعماله الخاصة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This comprehensive maxim continues the command to thank God by asking that His favors endure, as gratitude brings increase.
rows.anchor: عطف على تفريع الأمر بالشكر على النعم أمر بطلب استمرار نعم الله تعالى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raghiba ordinarily takes the desired object with fī and the one asked directly; raghiba an means turning away. Aisha reads the omitted preposition in 4:127 as an.
rows.anchor: والرغبة : طلب حصول ما هو محبوب وأصله أن يعدى إلى المطلوب منه بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ilā is used because irghab includes turning toward someone who has one's need, like a traveler heading to his destination; compare Abraham's statement.
rows.anchor: وأما تعدية فعل { فارغب } هنا بحرف { إلى } فلتضمينه معنى الإقبال والتوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting 'to your Lord' first makes desire exclusive to God, fitting the Messenger's supreme status; the omitted object encompasses all his aims, especially spiritual perfection, the spread of religion, and Muslim victory.
rows.anchor: وتقديم إلى { ربك } على { فارغب } لإفادة الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fā in fansab and farghab links the actions because fronted complements imply restriction and hence a conditional sense; Qur'anic examples show this pattern.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الفاء في قوله : { فانصب } ( الشرح : 7 ) وقوله : { فارغب } رابطة للفعل

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: When a man asked to join jihad, the Prophet asked whether his parents were alive and told him to strive by serving them.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمن سأل منه أن يخرج للجهاد

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi cites Ibn al-Shajari's puzzlement that waw and fā meet here, since fā ordinarily marks coordination, an answer, or a relative clause; Ibn Ashur says his analysis removes the puzzle.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطيبي عن ( أمالي السيد ) ( يعني ابن الشجري ) أن اجتماع الفاء والواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The olive is a familiar fruit yielding edible oil and lamp fuel; swearing by it, like the fig, points to God's attributes and to the benefits of a sustaining, useful creation.
rows.anchor: والزيتون أيضا ظاهرة الثمرة المشهورة ذات الزيت الذي يعتصر منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and several early authorities take the fig and olive literally, stressing their benefits as gifts to people.
rows.anchor: وعلى ظاهر الاسمين للتين والزيتون حملهما جمع من المفسرين الأولين ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas interprets the fig as Noah's mosque built on Mount Judi after the flood; Ibn Ashur suggests the mountain may be named for abundant fig trees.
rows.anchor: فروي عن ابن عباس أيضا تفسير التين بأنه مسجد نوح الذي بني على الجودي بعد الطوفان

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays's verse demonstrates naming a place by the tree abundant there, supporting the proposed place-name explanation of Tīn.
rows.anchor: كقول امرىء القيس : أمرخ ديارهم أم عشر

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha's poem names a place called al-Tin, offering another attestation of the place-name.
rows.anchor: وسمي بالتين موضع جاء في شعر النابغة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas and others identify al-Zaytun with the hill of Jerusalem's mosque, named for its olive trees.
rows.anchor: والزيتون يطلق على الجبل الذي بني عليه المسجد الأقصى لأنه ينبت الزيتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur also allows the oath to mean the fruit trees themselves, honored because many grow in these two sacred places, like Jareer praying for the beloved's basil tree.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يكون القسم ب { التين والزيتون } معنيا بهما شجر هاتين الثمرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tur Sinin is the known Sinai mountain; tur means mountain in Nabataean/Canaanite, and Sinin names its desert, a variant of Sin between Egypt and Palestine.
rows.anchor: وأما { طور سينين } فهو الجبل المعروف ب ( طور سينا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations derive Sinin from a word for trees in Nabataean or Abyssinian, or from an Abyssinian word meaning beautiful.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سينين اسم الأشجار بالنبطية أو بالحبشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinin is an Arabic loan that resembles a sound masculine plural but is not one; grammarians allow its inflection like that plural or its retention in yāʾ with case vowels on the nūn.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء تعريبه في العربية على صيغة تشبه صيغة جمع المذكر السالم وليس بجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure town is Mecca, called secure because entrants are safe; amīn may mean granting security or, by figurative attribution, that its inhabitants are protected.
rows.anchor: و { البلد الأمين } : مكة ، سمي الأمين لأن من دخله كان آمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative honors Mecca and treats it as visibly present to the audience because the surah descended there, as in the opening of Surat al-Balad.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إليه للتعظيم ولأن نزول السورة في ذلك البلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If fig and olive indicate sacred places, the oath can evoke Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Islam's laws; Jesus is omitted because his law completes the Torah.
rows.anchor: فالتين إيماء إلى رسالة نوح وهي أول شريعة لرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abraham built the Jerusalem mosque; this supports reading the olive as his law's place, followed by Sinai for Torah and Mecca for Islam.
rows.anchor: فإنه بنى المسجد الأقصى كما ورد في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Jerusalem can evoke Jesus's law, while the secure town evokes Abraham and Islam, whose foundations follow Abraham's hanif tradition; this yields Noah, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad out of historical order.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون الزيتون على تأويله بالمكان وبأنه المسجد الأقصى إيماء إلى مكان ظهور شريعة عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nonchronological order serves rhetorical pairing and wordplay: fruit names align with each other, place names with each other, and Sinin suits the surah's rhyme.
rows.anchor: فتوجيه مخالفة الترتيب الذكري للترتيب الخارجي أنه لمراعاة اقتران الاسمين المنقولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After excluding believers from being cast low, the text adds a tremendous reward; the indefinite form magnifies it.
rows.anchor: وفرع على معنى الاستثناء وهو أنهم ليسوا ممن يرد أسفل سافلين الإخبار بأن لهم أجرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mamnun can mean an unblemished reward on which no one reproaches the recipient, or a reward that is not cut off, from the word for severed rope.
rows.anchor: والممنون : الذي يمن على المأجور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transition follows the account of human creation and abasement: after believers are excepted, the remaining human is the denier of true religion.
rows.anchor: أي فقد بان لك أن غير الذين آمنوا هم الذين ردوا إلى أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma may be interrogative rebuke addressed to the human described earlier; direct address shifts from the expected third person to confront the denier more sharply.
rows.anchor: و ( ما ) يجوز أن تكون استفهامية ، والاستفهام توبيخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukadhdhibuka means 'make you a denier'; its omitted object is obvious and may be the Messenger, Islam, or resurrection and judgment.
rows.anchor: ومتعلق التكذيب : إما محذوف لظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Din may mean religion or law, as in two other verses; then the bāʾ is causal and the threat says God will judge those who deny the message or warned judgment.
rows.anchor: و { الدين } يجوز أن يكون بمعنى الملة والشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If understood as religion, the phrasing suggests the Quraysh did not accuse Muhammad of lying until he brought this new law.
rows.anchor: وأسلوب هذا التركيب مؤذن بأنهم لم يكونوا ينسبون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concluding question, 'Is God not the wisest judge?', begins a separate sentence serving as a threat and warning.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين } مستأنفة للتهديد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Din may instead mean retribution in the afterlife, as in two verses; here bā complements deny, as in other Qur'anic uses.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( الدين ) بمعنى الجزاء في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma may be a relative meaning 'the one who'; the Prophet is addressed, and the clause means someone accuses him of lying because of Islam or resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ( ما ) موصولة وما صدقها المكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complement after 'after' is omitted, understood as after the truth was made clear or after the person accepted his own low state.
rows.anchor: وحذف ما أضيف إليه { بعد } فبنيت بعد على الضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final question may predicate of the relative 'one' with an omitted 'in it,' or support an omitted threat that God will exact justice; the latter omits words because the question supplies the reason.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين } يجوز أن تكون خبرا عن ( ما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is confirmatory. Ahkam can derive from judgment, meaning most effective judge, or wisdom, meaning a ruling free from neglect of any benefit.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the best judge entails truth, crushing falsehood, and compelling those judged to comply, since the descriptive title invokes the qualities of judgment.
rows.anchor: وهي : إصابة الحق ، وقطع دابر الباطل ، وإلزام كل من يقضي عليه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet taught that readers who reach the final verse should answer, 'Yes indeed, and I am among those who testify.' Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud transmit it.
rows.anchor: روى الترمذي وأبو داود عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the first Qur'anic surah revealed was named by its opening words, Iqra bi-smi rabbika; several Successors transmit the same title, used by al-Tirmidhi.
rows.anchor: روي في ( المستدرك ) عن عائشة : ( أول سورة نزلت من القرآن اقرأ باسم ربك )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also commonly called al-Alaq because that word occurs near the beginning; Bukhari titles it Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq, and others call it Iqra or Iqra wa-l-Alaq.
rows.anchor: وسميت في المصاحف ومعظم التفاسير ( سورة العلق ) لوقوع لفظ ( العلق )

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya and Ibn al-Arabi call this surah al-Qalam, while those who do so call the other surah Nun; al-Suyuti does not list this one among surahs with multiple names.
rows.anchor: وعنونها ابن عطية وأبو بكر بن العربي : ( سورة القلم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan by agreement and was the first revealed; its first five verses came in Hira during Ramadan on the seventeenth, year forty after the Elephant, according to sound Aisha reports and most exegetes.
rows.anchor: وهي أول سورة نزلت في القرآن كما ثبت في الأحاديث الصحيحة الواضحة

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir says al-Muddaththir was first; Ibn Ashur reconciles this as the first revelation after the pause, like al-Duha after the second pause.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر أول سورة المدثر ، وتؤول بأن كلامه نص أن سورة المدثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse-count traditions give twenty verses in Medina and Mecca, eighteen in Syria, and nineteen in Kufa and Basra.
rows.anchor: وعدد آيها في عد أهل المدينة ومكة عشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah teaches Muhammad to recite Qur'anic speech though he did not previously know recitation, and suggests that God can directly enable knowledge as He enabled writing.
rows.anchor: تلقين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الكلام القرآني وتلاوته إذ كان لا يعرف التلاوة من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the first Qur'an revealed to Muhammad, as established in the forthcoming report from Aisha.
rows.anchor: هذا أول ما أوحي به من القرآن إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with 'Recite' announces that the Messenger will become a reciter of scripture although he had not recited scripture before revelation; it is a fitting opening for the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وافتتاح السورة بكلمة { اقرأ } إيذان بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيكون قارئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqra literally commands reading aloud of specified written or memorized words; the grammatical discussion parallels the command in al-Nahl.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { اقرأ } أمر بالقراءة ، والقراءة نطق بكلام معين مكتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative asks for immediate or near-future recitation of words about to be dictated, since no text had previously been read or handed to him.
rows.anchor: فالمطلوب بقوله : { اقرأ } أن يفعل القراءة في الحال أو المستقبل القريب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha narrates in the two Sahihs that Gabriel came to Muhammad in Hira, commanded him three times, embraced him forcefully each time, then recited the opening through 'what he did not know.'
rows.anchor: وفي حديث ( الصحيحين ) عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها فيه : ( حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aisha's narration is directly from the Prophet; her account that he returned trembling with the passage means he retained and recited what had been dictated.
rows.anchor: فهذا الحديث روته عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقولها قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khadija's request that Waraqa hear him further indicates Muhammad recited the revealed passage immediately; Gabriel's repeated command repeated God's wording to accustom him to reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا ينبىء بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عندما قيل له بعد الفطة الثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God 'the Creator' implies exclusive divinity: because He alone created, people should invoke Him rather than al-Lat or al-Uzza, though the polytheists acknowledged His creation of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: وجيء في وصف الرب بطريق الموصول { الذي خلق } ولأن في ذلك استدلالا على انفراد الله بالإلاهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Created the human from a clot' may be a detailed apposition to general creation, a partitive apposition if the first object is broad, or an explanation specifying that God created humans from clots.
rows.anchor: وجملة { خلق الإنسان من علق } يجوز أن تكون بدلا من جملة { الذي خلق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object after the first 'created' may be omitted because the verb is intransitive, to mean the Creator; omitted for generality, to mean all creation; or supplied by the next phrase as 'humanity.'
rows.anchor: وعدم ذكر مفعول لفعل { خلق } يجوز أن يكون لتنزيل الفعل منزلة اللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are singled out because each person readily reflects on their own origin, making it a compelling proof of the Creator.
rows.anchor: وخص خلق الإنسان بالذكر من بين بقية المخلوقات لأنه المطرد في مقام الاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implicitly censures polytheists for missing the proof of divine unity present in their own selves.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض بتحميق المشركين الذين ضلوا عن توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clot points to wondrous stages and qualities that make humanity sovereign over earthly creation.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { من علق } إشارة إلى ما ينطوي في أصل خلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alaq is the collective name for analaqah: a fingernail-sized, dark red, moist clot, named for resemblance to a small freshwater leech that attaches to animals and sucks blood.
rows.anchor: والعلق : اسم جمع علقة وهي قطعة قدر الأنملة من الدم الغليظ الجامد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After male and female fluids unite and time passes, they become a clot; it marks the start of formation because the male fluid alone cannot produce an embryo.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : { خلق الإنسان من علق } أن نطفة الذكر ونطفة المرأة بعد الاختلاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clot's later development into maturity encodes hidden capacities, especially the ability to gain knowledge and write.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن خلق الإنسان من علق ثم مصيره إلى كمال أشده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur calls mention of the clot a scientific miracle: the microscopic fertilized ovum develops in fluid, resembling a leech in size, blood color, and suspension, unless impeded.
rows.anchor: ومن إعجاز القرآن العلمي ذكر العلقة لأن الثابت في العلم الآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min denotes a starting point.
rows.anchor: ومعنى حرف { من } الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command to recite repeats the first to give it additional emphasis.
rows.anchor: وفعل { اقرأ } الثاني تأكيد ل { اقرأ } الأول للاهتمام بهذا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a new explanatory statement: Rabbuka is subject, with either 'who taught by the pen' or 'taught humanity what it did not know' as predicate.
rows.anchor: و { ربك } مبتدأ وخبره إما { الذي علم بالقلم } وإما جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without Aisha's revelation report, the statement answers Muhammad's presumed question about reading without literacy: the one who taught writing can teach what he does not know.
rows.anchor: كيف أقرأ وأنا لا أحسن القراءة والكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the hadith, the passage answers his 'I cannot read': God can teach by dictation, instruction, or inspiration, just as He taught Adam the names without literacy.
rows.anchor: إذ العلم بالقراءة يحصل بوسائل أخرى مثل الإملاء والتلقين والإلهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'your Lord' instead of using a pronoun stresses the care already implied in 'recite in your Lord's name' and marks reading as a special gift of lordship; it also leads into al-Akram.
rows.anchor: فعدل عن الإضمار لتأكيد ما يشعر به { ربك } من العناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akram intensifies generosity rather than comparing God with another; generosity is giving benefit, and God's favors begin with creation and its sustaining provision.
rows.anchor: ووصف { الأكرم } مصوغ للدلالة على قوة الاتصاف بالكرم وليس مصوغا للمفاضلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: lordship implies existence and oneness, creation and teaching indicate acts, and al-Akram entails perfection and freedom from deficiency.
rows.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلاهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two objects of 'taught by the pen' are omitted, understood as teaching writers or teaching people to write; Arabs prized literacy and associated it with scriptural communities.
rows.anchor: ومفعولا { علم بالقلم } محذوفان دل عليهما قوله : { بالقلم }

rows.speaker: أبو حية النميري
rows.claim: Abu Hayya's line about a Jew's hand supports the association of writing with Jews and skilled script.
rows.anchor: كما قال أبو حية النميري : كما خط الكتاب بكف يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poem boasts of learning writing though its speaker says he is no writer; writing first appeared among Arabs in Anbar, then reached Hijaz through Harb ibn Umayya, who learned from Aslam ibn Sidra, taught by Muramir ibn Murra; Himyar earlier used Musnad.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن ظهور الخط في العرب أول ما كان عند أهل الأنبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing 'who taught by the pen' between subject and predicate reassures the Prophet that the one who taught writing can teach him recitation though he cannot write.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص هذه الصلة بالذكر وجعلها معترضة بين المبتدإ والخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen is a sharpened reed used to draw ink on paper; the discussion also recalls pens cast to decide who would care for Mary.
rows.anchor: والقلم : شظية من قصب ترقق وتثقف وتبرى بالسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Taught humanity what it did not know' is the predicate of 'your Lord is most generous'; what comes between is parenthetical, and humanity is generic.
rows.anchor: وجملة : علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم } خبر عن قوله : { وربك الأكرم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human learning comes by three routes: written transmission and reading across peoples and generations, oral teaching or dictation, and intellectual deductions and inventions; the latter two are included in God's broad teaching.
rows.anchor: الأخذ عن الغير بالمراجعة ، والمطالعة ، وطريقهما الكتابة وقراءة الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reassures the Prophet that illiteracy cannot prevent recitation: God can teach him without prior skill in writing, as He teaches all previously unknown things.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك اطمئنان لنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن عدم معرفته الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording 'what he did not know' signals that knowledge follows a prior state of ignorance, so acquired learning is new to the learner.
rows.anchor: وأشعر قوله : { ما لم يعلم } أن العلم مسبوق بالجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse underscores the importance of writing and God's intention that the revelation be recorded; the Prophet therefore employed scribes from the start of his mission.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى الاهتمام بعلم الكتابة وبأن الله يريد أن يكتب للنبيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial command and reference to pen teaching imply that Muhammad remained unlettered, an attribute completing the Qur'an's miracle, as another verse states.
rows.anchor: وفي الاقتصار على أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقراءة ثم إخباره بأن الله علم الإنسان بالقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are the final five verses of the passage first revealed at Hira; the following discussion on verses 6–10 begins a new subject.
rows.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and invalidation; appearing before any obvious target indicates that the intended target follows, namely the one who forbids a servant from praying.
rows.anchor: وحرف { كلا } ردع وإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla normally follows the speech it rejects, but here it opens the sentence because the following statement is what deserves repudiation; Imru al-Qays offers a similar initial negative particle.
rows.anchor: وحق { كلا } أن تقع بعد كلام لإبطاله والزجر عن مضمونه

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Muslim transmits Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad's neck while praying; when he approached, he recoiled from a fiery trench and terror, and the Prophet said angels would have torn him apart. The report is linked to revelation of these verses, though its placement in Abu Hurayra's report is uncertain.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي حازم عن أبي هريرة قال : ( قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the verses beginning 'Have you seen the one who forbids' descended about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad during prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري : ذكر أن آية { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى } وما بعدها نزلت في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accounts can be reconciled: the passage beginning at 96:9 directly concerns Abu Jahl, while the statement about human transgression through 96:8 prepares for it.
rows.anchor: ووجه الجمع بين الروايتين : أن النازل في أبي جهل بعضه مقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes disagree whether these verses followed the first five immediately; prayer's mention seems problematic if obligatory prayer began at the Night Journey years later. Some posit intervening revelation and later attachment, while others deny this was the first revelation.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أن هذه الآيات إلى آخر السورة نزلت عقب الخمس الآيات الماضية
